source_findings.finding: The upstream OpenAI Realtime surface accepts conversation.item.truncate, but documents it as an acknowledgement-free no-op.
On cancelled, failed, or incomplete responses, ResponseHandler rolls back provisional generation from the internal Chat before deferred client items are applied.
Response lifecycle state tombstones closed response keys so late output from a cancelled response is intended to remain stale rather than reopen the response.
Current upstream main includes PR #523, preserving chat turn order during non-interrupting back-to-back speech via history anchors and anchored provisional-generation insertion.
Upstream explicitly describes its Agents SDK compatibility matrix as core GA compatibility, not full OpenAI Realtime API equivalence.

reconciliation.superseded_or_narrowed_hypothesis: conversation.item.truncate being absent or a no-op is by itself sufficient evidence that unheard assistant content leaks into next-turn server context
reconciliation.replacement_hypothesis: The no-op truncate may be safe for F2 only if response cancellation plus provisional-history rollback, response-key tombstoning, playback clearing and tool/result fencing jointly prevent every unheard or stale interrupted-turn semantic from influencing the next turn.
reconciliation.why: Source inspection shows a stronger rollback mechanism than the initial truncate-only concern, but source structure cannot prove real event ordering under concurrent playback, TTS, tool completion and reconnect races.

highest_information_next_discriminator.surface: lowest safe faithful VPS sandbox under existing Trigger4 execution authority
steps: Start one response that produces enough text/audio to create measurable generated-ahead-of-playback state.
Record generated transcript boundary, emitted audio boundary and F2 measured heard boundary independently.
Barge in while output is partially heard; send response.cancel and the transport-appropriate playback clear/truncate sequence.
Allow deliberately delayed cancelled-generation TTS/audio and a deliberately delayed old-turn tool result to arrive after cancellation.
Start the next user turn with a deterministic context-probe prompt and capture the exact model input/chat state used for that turn.
Fail if any cancelled-generation assistant semantic beyond F2 authority, any stale tool result, or any late audio regains current-turn authority.
Repeat across WebSocket and, separately, WebRTC because playback ownership and clear semantics differ.
